userStories.title: Classify wall-clock timeouts as fail-timeout
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Surface a wall-clock timeout as a transport fact and classify empty timed-out run output as `fail-timeout` without changing idle-agent behavior.

**Motivation** — A wall-clock timeout on an agent turn currently returns empty output, which the hop body synthesises into `fail-stale` — the outcome reserved for an *idle* agent.

**Approach** — Surface the timeout as a transport fact on `TurnResult` and map it to a policy outcome at the wiring layer, leaving the adapter free of policy naming (the convention `SessionTurnError` already documents). With only this story landed, a timeout produces a single hop and a terminal failure.

**Scope** — In: `TurnResult.timedOut`, ACP result assembly extraction, empty-output failure classification extraction, and fail-timeout mapping. Out: timeout retry policy and timeout retry prompting; No change to `fail-stale` semantics, its retry count, its category, its reason field, or the idle-watchdog path that produces it.

**Design notes** — `category: "quality", not "availability".` `shouldSwap` returns `true` for `availability`, and the swap path calls `markUnavailable(currentAgent, …)`, which prunes that agent for the remainder of the run. A single slow story would poison the agent pool for every subsequent story. `quality` routes to `fallback.onQualityFailure ?? false`, leaving swap opt-in. Move `sendTurn`'s result assembly into the existing `src/agents/acp/adapter-output.ts` as `buildTurnResult`, which then carries `timedOut`; move the existing empty-output synthesis verbatim into `src/operations/turn-failure-classification.ts`, then add the timeout branch. Each extraction must be net-negative.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface TurnResult {
  timedOut?: boolean;
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: When `sendTurn` returns because its wall-clock timeout elapsed, then its returned `TurnResult.timedOut` equals `true`.
When `sendTurn` returns because its wall-clock timeout elapsed, then its returned `TurnResult.output` equals the empty string.
When `sendTurn` returns normally within its budget, then `TurnResult.timedOut` is absent or `false`.
Given a turn result with empty output and `timedOut: true`, when failure classification runs, then `adapterFailure.outcome` equals `"fail-timeout"`.
Given a turn result with empty output and `timedOut: true`, when failure classification runs, then `adapterFailure.category` equals `"quality"`.
Given a turn result with empty output and `timedOut: true`, when failure classification runs, then `adapterFailure.retriable` equals `true`.
Given a turn result with empty output and `timedOut` false or absent, when failure classification runs, then `adapterFailure.outcome` equals `"fail-stale"`.
Given a turn result with empty output and `timedOut` false or absent, when failure classification runs, then `adapterFailure.reason` equals `"empty-output"`.
Given a turn result that already carries an `adapterFailure`, when `timedOut` is true, then failure classification preserves the existing failure.
When `shouldSwap` receives an `AdapterFailure` with outcome `"fail-timeout"`, category `"quality"`, and unset `agent.fallback.onQualityFailure`, then it returns `false`.
When `runWithFallback` receives a hop result whose `adapterFailure.outcome` is `"fail-timeout"`, then the dispatched agent is not recorded as unavailable for subsequent calls.

routing.reasoning: This is a bounded transport-to-policy change across existing adapters and operation wiring, with focused unit and manager integration coverage for the retained stale path.

userStories.title: Retry fail-timeout once with a reduced fresh-session budget
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a bounded, per-story `fail-timeout` retry that gets half the prior hop budget and always opens a fresh session.

**Motivation** — The manager then restarts the same agent up to three times, each with a full fresh timeout budget, so every timeout costs roughly four times its configured budget before reaching a terminal story failure.

**Approach** — Add a `fail-timeout` branch to `runWithFallback` with its own attempt counter, passing a reduced `timeoutSeconds` on the retry hop and opening a fresh session.

**Scope** — In: timeout retry config defaults, retry policy extraction, timeout retry accounting, reduced resolved run options, and fresh-session dispatch. Out: retry prompt progress guidance; Making wall-clock timeouts trigger tier escalation is out of scope. A timeout that exhausts its retry remains a terminal story failure via `runner.ts:87`, exactly as today.; and No change to `fail-stale` semantics, its retry count, its category, its reason field, or the idle-watchdog path that produces it.

**Design notes** — `A new timeout-retry hop kind, not a reuse of stale-retry.` `build-hop-callback.ts:182` resolves `stale-retry` by reusing the live session handle via `getLiveHandle`. A wall-clock timeout *terminated* the session, so reusing that variant would hand the retry a dead handle. `retriable: true.` The pre-existing contract test at `test/unit/agents/fail-stale-complete.test.ts:64` specifies `retriable: false` for a wall-clock timeout. That test constructs an object literal and asserts on it — it never exercises production code — so nothing breaks. This spec deliberately overrides that earlier intent on the grounds of cumulative on-disk progress, which the original design did not account for. Move the existing fail-stale retry block **verbatim** into a new `src/agents/retry/hop-retry-policy.ts`, then add the fail-timeout branch there. Net must leave `manager.ts` below its baseline entry.

**Interface**
```typescript
| { kind: "timeout-retry"; attempt: number }

agent.timeoutRetry.maxAttempts // default 1
agent.timeoutRetry.budgetMultiplier // default 0.5
```
acceptanceCriteria: When the first `runWithFallback` hop returns `fail-timeout`, then exactly one additional hop is dispatched by default.
When the first `runWithFallback` hop returns `fail-timeout`, then the additional hop receives `timeoutSeconds` equal to half the first hop's `timeoutSeconds`.
When the timeout-retry hop also returns `fail-timeout`, then no third hop is dispatched and `runWithFallback` returns a failing outcome.
When comparing `{ kind: "timeout-retry", attempt: 1 }` and `{ kind: "stale-retry", attempt: 1 }`, then their `kind` fields are distinguishable.
When `executeHop` is invoked with `{ kind: "timeout-retry" }`, then it opens a new session rather than reusing the cached live handle used by `stale-retry`.
When configuration is constructed with `agent.timeoutRetry.maxAttempts` unset, then the resolved value equals `1`.
When configuration is constructed with `agent.timeoutRetry.budgetMultiplier` unset, then the resolved value equals `0.5`.
When `agent.timeoutRetry.maxAttempts` is `0` and a hop returns `fail-timeout`, then exactly one hop is dispatched and no retry occurs.
When the first hop returns `fail-stale`, then same-agent retries dispatched equal `agent.idleWatchdog.maxRetryAttempts`.
When a `fail-timeout` outcome exhausts its retry budget, then the calling operation surfaces no output and follows the same terminal failure path as exhausted `fail-stale`.

routing.reasoning: The retry loop changes stateful fallback control flow, per-hop option propagation, and session reuse rules while preserving the independent stale retry policy.

userStories.title: Give timeout retries an informed progress prompt
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Rewrite only timeout-retry prompts with a generic timeout preamble plus git-derived guidance about work left on disk.

**Motivation** — Attempt 2 does not redo attempt 1, it continues from whatever landed on disk.

**Approach** — Compose the retry prompt from a generic timeout preamble plus guidance conditioned on whether the working tree changed during the timed-out attempt.

**Scope** — In: `timeoutRetry` prompt builder helper and barrel export, pre-attempt git reference capture, working-tree changed-file detection against that ref, elapsed-duration text, and callback dependency injection. Out: Permanent changes to the test-writer's standing prompt are deferred; the only prompt change is the retry-time injection defined here.; Preserving an agent's partial message output across a timeout is deferred; `extractOutput` continues to yield `""` when the turn timed out.; Disk-based recovery of an op's deliverable is deferred; no op gains an `op.recover` hook, and artifact presence is never treated as completion.; and any prompt rewrite for `primary` or `stale-retry`.

**Design notes** — Prompt authoring stays inside `src/prompts/builders/` as `forbidden-patterns.md` requires; `rectifier-builder-helpers.ts` is the established sibling pattern for helper functions in that directory, and `timeoutRetry` is re-exported from the `src/prompts` barrel. Use the pre-attempt ref with a working-tree diff so uncommitted edits from the timed-out session are included. Pre-attempt git ref unavailable or capture fails: Retry prompt degrades to the generic preamble; no throw.
acceptanceCriteria: When `timeoutRetry` is imported from the `src/prompts` barrel and called, then its returned string includes the original prompt text.

Given a non-empty list of changed file paths, when `timeoutRetry` builds a prompt, then the returned prompt names each path and instructs the agent to continue from the existing state rather than restart.

Given an empty list of changed file paths, when `timeoutRetry` builds a prompt, then the returned prompt states that the previous attempt produced no file changes and instructs the agent to change its approach.
Given an empty list of changed file paths, when `timeoutRetry` builds a prompt, then the returned prompt does not instruct the agent to continue from existing work.
When `timeoutRetry` builds a prompt, then the returned prompt states the elapsed duration of the timed-out attempt.

When the `executeHop` closure is invoked with a `timeout-retry` hop kind, then the `timeoutRetry` entry substituted on `_buildHopCallbackDeps` is called exactly once with the original prompt and the list of changed file paths.
When the `executeHop` closure is invoked with a `primary` or `stale-retry` hop kind, then the `timeoutRetry` entry on `_buildHopCallbackDeps` is not called.
When the pre-attempt git reference is unavailable, then timeout retry prompt construction resolves to a prompt containing the generic timeout preamble without throwing.

routing.reasoning: This extends an existing callback seam and pure prompt-helper pattern with a bounded git-state observation and focused primary/stale non-regression checks.

analysis:
This is an enhancement to the ACP run-kind operation path, not a greenfield feature. `AcpAgentAdapter.sendTurn` records `timedOut` locally after `runSessionPrompt` but currently returns only extracted empty output, so the transport fact is lost (src/agents/acp/adapter.ts:435-626). `TurnResult` already carries transport output, cost, interactions, and an optional policy-level `adapterFailure` (src/agents/types.ts:444-472); add optional `timedOut` there without putting policy terminology in the adapter. `callOp` owns the run-hop body and currently synthesizes retriable availability `fail-stale` for empty effective output when no adapter failure exists (src/operations/call.ts:304-334); extract this classification into `src/operations/turn-failure-classification.ts`, preserve the fail-stale branch verbatim, and map only empty timed-out results to retriable quality `fail-timeout`. `AdapterFailure` already declares `fail-timeout` as a quality outcome (src/context/engine/types.ts:22-65).

`AgentManager.runWithFallback` controls same-agent stale retries, swaps, fallback records, and terminal outcomes (src/agents/manager.ts:222-464). Its existing fail-stale branch performs immediate same-agent retries governed by `agent.idleWatchdog.maxRetryAttempts`; move that block verbatim into a focused retry-policy module before adding independent timeout attempts. The timeout retry must pass a copied per-hop `AgentRunOptions` whose `timeoutSeconds` is the preceding hop budget times `agent.timeoutRetry.budgetMultiplier`, default 0.5, and must not mark the agent unavailable: `shouldSwap` only swaps quality failures when `fallback.onQualityFailure` is opted in. Add `timeoutRetry` defaults to the Zod agent schema and its root default object (src/config/schemas-infra.ts:227-260; src/config/schemas.ts:343-355). `HopKind` currently distinguishes `primary`, session-reusing `stale-retry`, and `swap` (src/agents/manager-types.ts:13-18); add `timeout-retry` so the callback can open a fresh session.

`buildHopCallback` builds prompts and opens sessions per hop (src/operations/build-hop-callback.ts:85-298). It intentionally reuses `getLiveHandle` only for `stale-retry`; timeout-retry must follow the fresh-session path, receive the reduced resolved options, and invoke an injected `timeoutRetry` prompt helper exactly once. Capture the git ref before the timed-out primary attempt, compare the working tree against it after timeout, and degrade safely if ref capture fails. Keep prompt authoring in `src/prompts/builders/rectifier-builder-helpers.ts` and re-export from `src/prompts/index.ts`; `captureGitRef` already returns `undefined` rather than throwing on git failures (src/utils/git.ts:90-98).

Existing tests establish the primary seams: ACP timeout behavior is covered in `test/unit/agents/acp/adapter-phase-a.test.ts:176-190`; empty-output operation behavior is in `test/unit/operations/call.test.ts`; stale manager semantics are comprehensively covered by `test/unit/agents/fail-stale-agent-manager.test.ts`; live-session reuse is integration-tested in `test/integration/agents/stale-retry-session-reuse.test.ts:1-115`; and callback dependency substitution is covered by `test/unit/operations/build-hop-callback.test.ts`. Add or extend focused unit and integration tests in these neighborhoods. Main risks are accidentally changing fail-stale retry count/category/reason, making timeout invoke the availability swap path and poisoning the agent pool, reusing a dead session, misapplying the timeout multiplier to the original rather than next hop, and violating the file-size ratchet. Migration is additive and configuration-compatible: absent timeoutRetry settings resolve to one retry at half budget; existing idleWatchdog configuration remains the sole control for fail-stale. No baseline bump is permitted: extract net-negative code from adapter.ts, call.ts, and manager.ts into the named helpers/modules.
outOfScope: Repetition or tool-call-loop detection (signature hashing of repeated tool calls) is deferred; this spec does not detect that an agent is looping, only that it exceeded its budget.
A per-turn tool-call ceiling is deferred; the number of tool calls within a single turn remains unbounded.
Disk-based recovery of an op's deliverable is deferred; no op gains an `op.recover` hook, and artifact presence is never treated as completion.
Preserving an agent's partial message output across a timeout is deferred; `extractOutput` continues to yield `""` when the turn timed out.
Permanent changes to the test-writer's standing prompt are deferred; the only prompt change is the retry-time injection defined here.
Making wall-clock timeouts trigger tier escalation is out of scope. A timeout that exhausts its retry remains a terminal story failure via `runner.ts:87`, exactly as today.
The `complete`-kind timeout path is out of scope; `adapter.complete` throws `AGENT_TIMEOUT` (`adapter.ts:190`) and never entered the fail-stale ladder.

The `_runHop` / `session-run-hop` dispatch path is out of scope. It constructs results with `success: true` unconditionally (`session-run-hop.ts:74`) and so reports a timeout as success — a separate latent defect requiring its own spec.
No change to `fail-stale` semantics, its retry count, its category, its reason field, or the idle-watchdog path that produces it.
US-003 only: concurrent timeout retries across parallel stories share no counter state; each `runWithFallback` call owns its own attempt count, and cross-story rate limiting of timeouts is deferred.
